classification.difficultyReason: Use the angle from east to establish the forward bearing, then parallel north references and angles at a point to find the reverse bearing.

content.prompt: What is the true bearing of $A$ from $B$?

spec.description: North and east reference arrows at A, short leftward and downward extensions, and AB extending southeast with its supplied 25-degree angle below east.
spec.mathematics: AB is 25 degrees south of east, so its bearing from A is 115 degrees. B is placed using offset (3.5 sin 115 degrees, 3.5 cos 115 degrees); no distance is given.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 25-degree angle is visible. No reverse-bearing arc or answer is included.

answer.worked:
The bearing of $B$ from $A$ is
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Bearing of }B\text{ from }A &= 90^{\circ}+25^{\circ}\\\text{Bearing of }B\text{ from }A &= 115^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$$
The smaller angle between north at $B$ and $BA$ is
$$\begin{aligned}\theta &= 180^{\circ}-115^{\circ}\\\theta &= 65^{\circ}\end{aligned}$$
by cointerior angles on parallel north references. The clockwise bearing of $A$ from $B$ is
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Bearing} &= 360^{\circ}-65^{\circ}\\\text{Bearing} &= 295^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$$
